name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+12 partisan lean in a Democratic-leaning state
Luke Bronin's large fundraising advantage over Amy Chai
Prediction markets price Democratic win around 95%
Open seat removes incumbent-specific risk but no polling available
model.rationale: The district's D+12 lean, Bronin's roughly 150-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 95% all point the same way, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of about 20 points. With no polls and an open seat, uncertainty is kept slightly wider than a typical safe race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a tighter-than-expected race, or a surge of outside spending for Chai, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's first district is an open seat after John Larson lost renomination, with Hartford mayor Luke Bronin carrying the Democratic banner against Republican Amy Chai. The district leans Democratic by about twelve points, and Bronin has raised over three million dollars with substantial outside support, while Chai has raised only about twenty thousand dollars. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance near 95 percent.

No general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. The expected margin is roughly twenty points Democratic, with modest extra uncertainty because this is an open seat and polling is absent.
